newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian-Uzbek grain-for-cotton barter deal falters.
newsitem.headline: Russian-Uzbek grain-for-cotton barter deal falters.

text.p: A deal in which Russia would barter 300,000 tonnes of food wheat for Uzbek cotton has stalled because Russia cannot come up with the grain, a senior trade source said on Monday.
The source, who asked not to be identified, said Russia had delivered about 22,000 tonnes of wheat under the scheme earlier this year but that future deliveries were in doubt.

The Central Asian state of Uzbekistan, the world's second largest cotton exporter, was unwilling to source grain in Kazakhstan, which has extra supplies, due to unspecified political reasons, the source said.
Uzbekistan's net grain harvest last year was a disastrous 2.7 million tonnes. Annual demand in the former Soviet republic is 3.5-4.0 million tonnes.
Russia's net 1996 grain harvest of 69.3 million tonnes was the second worst in three decades.

The source said an unnamed Russian oil company was responsible for the Russian end of the deal, but that it could not come up with financing to buy milling wheat, which the Uzbeks had insisted be of Russian origin.
The original barter volumes were set in an intergovernmental decree at 400,000 tonnes of wheat for about 77,000 tonnes of cotton, but had been reduced, the source said.
Uzbekistan said last month that it would import up to 1.2 million tonnes of wheat this year, mainly through Western commodities houses.
